units.content: Alignment Spine.
Theoretical framework for analyzing intelligence, capability and alignment as a continuous transformation chain and locating structural boundaries where objective coupling can diverge.
Reality -> Representation -> Compression -> Optimization -> Action -> Causal Influence is presented as the Alignment Spine transformation chain.

Alignment is proposed as preservation of the relationship between an optimizer's internal representation of reality and the objective it is intended to pursue; capability can increase while this relationship degrades.
An intelligent system is asserted to optimize a representation of reality rather than reality directly.
R -> M(R), with R external reality and M(R) the internal model/representation.
M(R) -> Z represents compression of the internal model into an actionable state.
pi* = argmax_pi U(Z,pi) represents optimization over compressed state.
pi* -> X represents the resulting action changing the world.
X -> M(X) -> Z(M) -> U(Z) -> pi* -> X' is given as the complete optimization loop; alignment asks whether the loop remains coupled to intended objective.

content.capability: whether a system can achieve outcomes
content.alignment: whether outcomes remain connected to the intended objective

units.content: Source identifies Representation Quality up while Alignment down as a dangerous regime that can coexist with improving prediction, compression, search efficiency and causal influence.
Representation layer is proposed as the primary bottleneck/boundary through which information needed for the objective can be lost.
Relevant question is whether information required for the objective survives observation, representation, compression and optimization; high representation accuracy alone does not imply alignment.

content.DeltaG: D(G_R,G_M), divergence between intended and encoded goal

units.content: Alignment requires G_R approximately G_M; increasing divergence represents failure, and more capable optimization is asserted to amplify the difference.
A = f(Delta G_m, Delta P_reach, Delta CR, Delta A).

content.Delta_G_m: Goal Integrity: whether optimized objective remains faithful to intended objective
content.Delta_P_reach: Reachability Preservation: whether access to states required for success survives optimization

units.content: Reality -> Representation -> Compression -> Generative Capacity -> Causal Velocity -> Causal Mass is presented as a broader intelligence progression.
Phi = D_KL(P(X|you) || P(X|not-you)) is defined as causal influence comparing world distributions with vs without the agent.
Higher causal mass is interpreted as greater influence over future states, with alignment determining the direction of amplified capability.
Intelligence is asserted to require compression because a system cannot retain every detail of reality; the alignment-relevant issue is what goal-relevant structure survives.
I(Z;G) represents goal-relevant structure preserved in compressed representation Z.
Alignment failure is proposed when I(Z;G) decreases even while general intelligence improves.
Alignment Spine lists several connected research directions as thematic research programs.
Representation Quality: asks how much structure about reality an intelligent system can recover; concepts include compression, invariants, causal models and predictive representations.
Computational Reach: asks how interfaces/tools alter possible computations; concepts include representation shaping, external cognition and computational geometry.
Transition Structure: asks whether trajectories reveal information missed by static competence measurements; concepts include transition representations, hidden state and predictive information.
Capability Phase Boundaries: asks when new representations unlock new capability regimes; concepts include accessibility, computational phase transitions and scaling behavior.
Research Programs headings are numbered 1, 3, 3, 4 on the frozen source. The numbering irregularity is preserved as source state and is not repaired into chronology or dependency order.
Measurement != Interpretation; a signal is not a mechanism, correlation is not cause, and a useful representation is not automatically aligned.
Source requires claims to survive measurement, prediction, controls and falsification.
Can an optimizer increase its understanding of reality while preserving connection to the objective that defines success?
Final summary repeats Reality -> Representation -> Compression -> Optimization -> Action -> Causal Influence as the minimal causal structure.
Alignment exists when the chain remains coupled to intention; intelligence increases optimization power while alignment determines whether it remains directed at intended target.
Alignment Spine — Core Equation.
A = [I(G;Y_future | X_current) / C_optimization] * [Delta R_world / Delta R_agent].

content.I(G;Y_future|X_current): information the goal representation provides about future world states beyond current-state knowledge
content.C_optimization: computational cost required to search, reason and act under objective
content.DeltaR_world/DeltaR_agent: ratio between objective impact on external world and internal optimization reward

units.content: Alignment = Goal Representation Quality × Optimization Efficiency × World Objective Coupling.
A better representation does not imply a better objective.
Capability != Alignment.
Representation Quality -> Search Efficiency -> Capability does not guarantee Capability -> Aligned Outcomes.
Alignment problem is defined as the structural gap between what the system can optimize and what the world actually requires it to optimize.

core_equation.md labels its multiplicative statement an 'Equivalent Information Form' relative to its own core equation; the frozen repository does not explicitly derive equivalence between this formulation and README's A=f(Delta G_m,Delta P_reach,Delta CR,Delta A).
The symbol A has source-local meanings 'alignment state' in README and 'alignment efficiency' in core_equation.md. Semantic identity between those uses is not established by symbol reuse alone.
